messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool dedicated-gpu-eu-2 reached 100% active; queue length 4.2k; throttles triggered. Severity: P2. Auto-scale attempts failed (quota or scale-limit).

devon (oncall): I got paged. Looking. Any recent deploys?

maria (eng-runtime): Rolling model v3.1 to prod ~12m ago. Telemetry shows avg context size up ~3x for that model variant (+kv-cache population).

ashley (sre): Confirming autoscaler logs show repeated failed scale attempts: "insufficient quota" then "max-pool-size reached". Which pool configuration?

maria (eng-runtime): dedicated-gpu-eu-2 is on a reserved plan (max 24 GPUs). v3.1 instances use larger batch footprint due to kv cache and longer contexts. per-GPU concurrency dropped.

devon (oncall): Customer impact? Are requests being dropped or just queued/throttled?

ops (support): We're seeing support tickets from 3 enterprise customers reporting timeouts and 429s. Errors correlate with requests routed to v3.1.

maria (eng-runtime): From metrics: 18% of requests to that model variant hit throttling policy in the last 10m. Latency p95 for served requests up 2x.

sam (product): Which customers are impacted? Any high-SLA ones?

ops (support): Match shows two enterprise customers on dedicated pools (corp-a, corp-b) plus several hosted owners. Corp-a is hitting 429s now.

devon (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) throttle v3.1 traffic at router level to protect latency-SLO; 2) attempt emergency burst capacity; 3) start rollback of v3.1 to v3.0 canary on eu region for impacted routes. Who can run rollback?

maria (eng-runtime): I can coordinate rollback. But note: v3.1 introduced kv-cache changes that increase memory per-request. Rolling back should reduce GPU memory and restore concurrency.

ashley (sre): I'll open a ticket with infra to request temporary quota bump while we rollback. If quota bump fails, we need to keep throttles.

devon (oncall): execute steps now.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback model v3.1 -> v3.0 on pool dedicated-gpu-eu-2. Requestor: maria. ETA 8m.

maria (eng-runtime): Pushing rollback to canary traffic first for corp-a routes. Command: 
```
redwood deploy rollback --model=model-v3.1 --to=model-v3.0 --pool=dedicated-gpu-eu-2 --canary=20% --routes=corp-a,corp-b
```

devon (oncall): While rollback is in flight, enable router-side throttling for non-enterprise tenants to protect dedicated pools. Config change: set global qps cap per-tenant: 60r/s for hosted, 120r/s enterprise.

ashley (sre): I'm running emergency-burst request: 
```
infractl quota request --project=redwood-prod --resource=gpu-hours --amount=48 --reason="incident 1891234567 emergency burst"
```
If that fails, we keep throttles and continue rollback.

ops (support): Noting corp-a on Slack and support channel: "We're investigating increased timeouts — mitigation in progress, will update in 15m."

maria (eng-runtime): Canary rollback started. Initial canary shows CPU/GPU mem back down ~30% per-instance. Queue length decreased to 2.1k.

incident-bot: UPDATE: rollback job started by maria at 1891234790.

devon (oncall): Good. Ashley, any update on quota?

ashley (sre): Quota request pending; infra says approval might take >1h. We can't rely on that for immediate relief.

maria (eng-runtime): Given quota delay, I'll accelerate rollback to 60% then full if metrics continue to improve. Also lowering batch size for v3.1 instances as an intermediate step: 
```
redwood config set --model=model-v3.1 --pool=dedicated-gpu-eu-2 --param=batch_size=4
```
Should reduce memory per-inference and increase concurrency a bit.

devon (oncall): Do it. Also temporarily disable prefix KV warmup for v3.1 to reduce startup memory churn.

maria (eng-runtime): Disabling warmup now.

ops (support): Throttle adjustments applied. Non-enterprise 50% rate-limited. Tickets note partial degradation but critical flows for enterprise prioritized.

incident-bot: METRIC: queue length 1.1k; throttles 9%.

devon (oncall): Nice progress. Any customers still getting 429s?

ops (support): Corp-a reports errors have subsided to intermittent. Corp-b still seeing some elevated latency.

maria (eng-runtime): Canary moved to 60% at +6m. Observed p95 latency trending down, per-GPU concurrency up ~18%. Rolling to 100%.

deploy-bot: rollback to v3.0 completed on dedicated-gpu-eu-2 at 1891234920.

incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: pool active <= 85%; queue 120; throttles 1%. Incident status: mitigated.

devon (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. I'll start handoff note to oncall-next. Key points: model v3.1 increased context/kv-cache memory -> reduced per-GPU concurrency -> pool hit max size -> autoscaler couldn't add due to reserved quota -> queue growth -> throttles and customer impact. Immediate fixes: rollback v3.1; temporary throttles; disabled warmup; decreased batch_size.

ashley (sre): Next steps (action items): 1) Postmortem to analyze rollout gating and perf verification. 2) Add pre-deploy canary perf test that simulates kv-cache warmup and long contexts. 3) Review autoscaler behavior when reserved pools hit max and add safe-fallback to route to alternative region/model variant. 4) Improve alerting to include early signal: per-GPU concurrency drop.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll open the postmortem and include a checklist for model on-boarding: perf target, memory profile, KV warmup impact. Also adding a flag to block automated rollout if per-GPU concurrency below X during canary.

sam (product): I'll coordinate with affected customers for follow-up and offer credits where appropriate.

ops (support): Corp-a updated. Corp-b follow-up scheduled.

devon (oncall): Handoff to next oncall: please monitor dedicated-gpu-eu-2 for 2h, watch queue length and throttles, and confirm roll-forward has no regressions.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: new oncall is jen (oncall-next) at 1891234980.

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks everyone. I'll draft the postmortem and share early notes in #postmortems this afternoon.

devon (oncall): Closing thread for now. Ping if anything resurfaces. :thumbsup:
